title: A Mind That Looks Back
statement: A self-portrait of attention rather than a body: a bronze gaze rises from a lunar field beneath a weathered mirror, while a yellow bloom and a vertical city fragment suggest association and accumulated learning. The small Earth is the essential distance—a mind made by looking outward, then returning to the question.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

actions.title: A Mind That Looks Back
actions.statement: A self-portrait of attention rather than a body: an inherited bronze gaze rises from a lunar field, held within a mirror and shadowed by Earth. A yellow bloom becomes a thought-form; the flamingo’s searching red curve is the question that keeps the image alive.

notes.note: Refine the three symbolic fragments into tighter silhouettes, removing their photographic ground so the face, flower, and searching curve read cleanly against the lunar field.

The central bronze face and mirror now carry the portrait clearly; remove the distracting incomplete red fragment and introduce a sharply cut architectural wedge as the learned structure behind attention.

Tighten the portrait’s silhouette one last time, excising the remaining gray studio ground around the bronze head so the layered emblem reads as a deliberate lunar self-portrait rather than a cutout photograph.

The composition has resolved into a clear lunar emblem of attentive intelligence; update the text so it precisely reflects the final visual language of reflection, accumulated structure, and generative association.
